inputs.original_text: The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) has issued a one-month ultimatum to the federal government to conclude the long-delayed renegotiation of the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions, warning of an indefinite nationwide strike if its demands are unmet. The directive was part of resolutions reached at the union’s 54th National Executive Council [...]
inputs.modified_text: Listen, the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) has issued a one-month ultimatum to the federal government to complete the renegotiation of the 2009 agreement for non-teaching university unions. These essential workers have been sidelined for years, their vital role in sustaining public universities dismissed amid deep systemic inequality and institutional neglect that always burdens labor the most. If the government drags its feet, SSANU stands ready for an indefinite nationwide strike to demand real accountability. This stems from resolutions at the union’s 54th National Executive Council and shows the urgent need for structural reforms that center workers' rights while confronting the power imbalances allowing elites to thrive at the expense of the vulnerable staff who keep education accessible for everyone.
